topic.readerProblem: A founder, marketer or analyst wants to know how often AI engines recommend their brand and how to count it correctly: which brands and answers belong in the denominator, how to resolve names, code rank, handle run-to-run variation and check what the answer actually claims.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity name a brand; this hub presents the benchmark built from those audit records and the coding rules, matching rules and small tools we use to turn raw answers into defensible numbers.

assessment: The page leads with AEOeye's refreshed recommendation benchmark (127 audits, 892 answers, 157 mentions, 17.6%) and its mandatory caveat, then gives a stepwise measurement method: eligibility, recommendation labels, entity resolution and alias matching, rank coding, repeat-run stability and engine agreement, claim-level accuracy, refusal and failure outcomes, and time-bound ground truth. It rests on AEOeye's own aggregates plus primary sources (SparkToro's 2,961-run study, FActScore, ALCE, the rank-biased overlap paper, Schema.org, OSF and standard reference definitions) and links five downloadable artifacts. It deliberately does not rank engines by mention rate, claim any repeat-run stability result of its own, present the synthetic fixtures as measurements, or call the labels an industry standard.

sources.supports: 600 volunteers ran 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI 2,961 times (November-December 2025); under 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice and about 1 in 1,000 for the same order; visibility percentage across many runs judged reasonable and ranking position not; suggests asking at least 60-100 times; author discloses help from Gumshoe.ai, an AI tracking startup.
FActScore breaks a generation into atomic facts and computes the percentage supported by a reliable knowledge source, because generations mix supported and unsupported information.
ALCE benchmark measures fluency, correctness and citation quality; on the ELI5 dataset even the best models lack complete citation support 50% of the time.

Author's version of Webber, Moffat and Zobel: rank-biased overlap compares incomplete rankings, weights high ranks more, and has a parameter that sets the strength of top-rank weighting (the ACM page returned 403, so the authors' PDF was read).
sameAs is the URL of a reference web page, such as a Wikipedia or Wikidata entry or official website, that unambiguously indicates the item's identity.
Preregistration is posting a time-stamped, read-only version of a study plan to a public repository before data collection or analysis.
PRISMA 2020 provides template flow diagrams for original and updated reviews (PRISMA is the reporting guideline for systematic reviews), cited as the reporting analogy for an eligibility funnel.
Each Wikidata entity has an ID prefixed by a letter; items are Q-items such as Q12345.
Normalization Form KC (NFKC) is compatibility decomposition followed by canonical composition.
Cohen's kappa measures inter-rater reliability for categorical data and, unlike simple percent agreement, accounts for agreement occurring by chance.
Standard competition ranking gives tied items the same number and leaves a gap (1224); dense ranking gives the next item the immediately following number (1223).
The reciprocal rank is the multiplicative inverse of the rank of the first correct answer; mean reciprocal rank averages it over queries.
Precision, recall and the F measure are set-based measures computed on unordered sets of documents and must be extended for ranked results.
Jaccard index is the intersection size divided by the union size of two sets.
Bootstrapping estimates the distribution of an estimator by resampling the data, often with replacement, and yields measures of accuracy such as confidence intervals.

artifacts.description: Answer-level aggregates of AEOeye's recommendation benchmark (127 audits, 892 answers) with per-engine figures, caveats and the previous snapshot.
Dependency-free Python regression corpus of 24 synthetic alias cases with a byte-checked expected output for exact and normalized brand matching.
Python generator that turns coded answer-brand rows into a weighted brand-pair edge list and node table, with synthetic fixture and expected outputs.
Browser-only calculator for repeat-run exact-set agreement, pairwise Jaccard, per-brand coverage and a seeded bootstrap interval; uploads nothing.
Python tool and synthetic before/after snapshots that diff two coded exports on prompt_id plus engine and report field changes and prompt-set gaps.

methodology: Benchmark: completed AEOeye audits created 2026-06-26 to 2026-09-07, extracted read-only on 2026-10-03; 127 audits after excluding 3 example, test, internal or localhost rows; unit is one engine answering one buyer question in one audit; a brand counts as mentioned when AEOeye's analysis model judged that the answer named it, and the result was stored per answer; repeat audits are kept and only aggregates are published. The measurement method is built from the codebooks, protocols and tools of the 16 merged pages and checked against external primary sources and standard definitions.
limitations: Self-selected brands with repeat audits; unequal engine samples that are not comparable (the free audit ran on Claude only until mid-2026); four engines have fewer than 10 mentions; mention judgments come from an analysis model rather than human coders; four of the five artifacts use synthetic data, and the labels are AEOeye proposals, not standards.
